En 1929 el matemático estadounidense Les: In 1929 the American mathematician Lester Hill published a cipher made with matrices: the letters are written as numbers from 0 to 25, grouped into vectors and multiplied by a key matrix. To decipher you have to multiply by the inverse matrix, and the key is only any use if that inverse exists. Hill even patented a machine of gears that did it. It was not much used, but it was the first time linear algebra entered cryptography wholesale, and cryptography today is made almost entirely of mathematics.
Resolver $AX = B$ es lo que hace un prog: Solving $AX = B$ is what a program does when it adjusts the colour of an image, corrects the perspective of a photo of a document or works out how forces are shared in a bridge. And the powers of a matrix are the way to see the future of a system that evolves step by step: if $A$ says how a population changes from one year to the next, $A^{50}$ says how it will be in fifty years. It is the idea developed in the topic on [[av-markov|Markov chains]].
